ai.description: *Indirana yadera* is a small frog (25–30 mm) with a brown dorsum and dark lateral bands. It is distinguished by a pointed snout and prominent, fleshy toe pads. It inhabits wet rock surfaces.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Indirana yadera* is best distinguished by the distinct, pale-colored longitudinal stripe running along the center of its back, which is absent in most similar species.
ai.habitat: *Indirana yadera* inhabits the leaf litter of evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Yadera Leaping Frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining active at night to forage for small invertebrates along the rocky, mossy streams of the Western Ghats.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Indirana yadera* breeds during the monsoon season, laying eggs in terrestrial clutches on wet rocks near streams. Development is direct, bypassing the free-swimming tadpole stage.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Indirana yadera* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically restricted to high-elevation evergreen forests in the state of Kerala.
ai.callDescription: The Yadera Leaping Frog produces a series of short, high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes, typically heard near rocky streams within its forest habitat.
